title: Screacher SC01 "Hollow Commuter" (a headless commuter in a torn suit jacket, shirt and tie) - rigged runtime derivative of the accepted Meshy T2.5 model (prototype)

family.name: Hollow Commuter
family.note: one enemy type with four visual variants: the same AI, stats and clip contract (names / durations / timings); each variant has its own skeleton fit and its own clip sampling

status.stage: generated by Meshy (image-to-3D of the user-approved concept); rig, skin weights and clips are local and procedural; not approved in game by a human yet
status.licenseClearance: none - a derivative of an AI generation (Meshy, conditioned on a Codex-generated image); access to it grants no licence, commercial or production clearance

honesty.rig: NEW derivative skeleton (shared 18-joint naming / hierarchy of the zombie wardrobe) and automatic skin weights created by this CPU pipeline
honesty.animation: hand-authored procedural keyframes / gait functions (lib/screacher-clips.mjs) sampled with this body's own joint positions - NOT motion capture
honesty.textures: the provider's own generated maps, resized / re-encoded only (no painting, no reprojection, no new artwork)
honesty.mesh: the mesh as generated (uniform scale + translation only): no decimation, no re-pose, no added geometry; there is no head and the neck stump is left open exactly as generated
honesty.generation: no AI generation, inference, model download or network service was used by this builder; the Meshy model was generated earlier by the task lead

provenance: generated (Meshy T2.5 image-to-3D, smart topology, 2K PBR, from the project's own user-approved Codex-generated concept image) + local derivative work; public provenance is hash-only

source.rawKeptOutsideGit: the raw GLB, the provider map files and the conditioning image are kept in a private raw-asset store outside Git (not modified, not shipped); only their hashes are public

meshy.poseNote: no pose mode requested: the model keeps the pose of the input image (arms hanging), which is the approved posture

inputImage.what: the user-approved concept image of this variant (the project's own Codex native image generation)

glb.format: glTF 2.0 binary; KHR_mesh_quantization (NORMAL int8 normalized; required); JPEG textures; JOINTS_0 u8 / WEIGHTS_0 normalized u8; one SkinnedMesh node

metallicRoughness.format: JPEG 4:4:4 (source packed map: G roughness, B metallic; resized)

normal.format: JPEG 4:4:4 tangent-space (source map resized; glTF convention, no tangents: three.js derivative tangents)

conventions.heightIs: floor -> top of the neck stump (there is no head)
conventions.bindPose: the relaxed pose as generated (legs vertical, arms hanging at the sides): no re-posing
conventions.bindRotations: identity (bone frames aligned with model space)

placement.note: scaled to 2 m; source faced +Z: no rotation; feet midpoint (bbox centres of soles below 4 cm) moved to origin

facing.method: sole bbox z-centre (lowest 3% of height) vs shin centroid (8-12%): toes extend toward the front

skeleton.headless: Neck = the base of the neck stump between the shoulders; Head = a TECHNICAL joint just under the top of the stump (the runtime ragdoll / actors look bones up by name); there is no head geometry, no head sphere and no head hit volume
skeleton.validationNote: the anthropometric ranges of autorig.validateSkeleton are for ordinary adults WITH a head measured to the crown; this body is headless (its height ends at the stump) and deliberately long-shinned / long-armed, so the listed out-of-range ratios are the generated proportions, not a detection failure (see the joint overlay sheet)

feet.method: generic (zombie/lib/skeleton.mjs) on the mesh cross-sections: foot depth widens > 1.3x shin depth below the ankle; joint 1.5 cm under the transition, clamped 0.07..0.13 m

legs.method: crotch = lowest height where a cross-section loop spans both legs (3 consecutive slices); hip height = 0.58 H (family proportion) clamped to crotch + [0.03, 0.16] m; hip x = 0.8 x thigh section centre 4 cm below the crotch (generic), hip z = thigh centreline (crotch - 0.22 .. - 0.04 m) extrapolated to the hip height; knee height = 0.395 H (the family's long-shin proportion, measured on the bare knees of SC04 and through the torn knees of SC02; trousers hide the knees of the others), centred in the leg section; ankle centred in the shin section

arms.method: per side: the arm cross-section loops (mesh-connected, not spanning the midline) tracked from the clearest mid-arm section (largest gap to the body) up while a separate loop exists (track tolerance 0.05 m: a sleeve tube and the arm inside it are separate loops at the same place); cloth armpit = first height where the body loop reaches over the tracked arm centre; below it the arm is the mesh piece flooded from the seed loop under the armpit height (every finger / thumb loop belongs to it exactly; the build stops if that flood reaches the midline); hand tip = lowest vertex under the lowest sections; wrist = the lowest section 0.14..0.36 m above the tip within 1.12 x the thinnest there (section size = sqrt(width x depth)); shoulder = the upper-arm centreline (line fit of the section centres from 4 cm above the elbow up) at 0.055 m under the shoulder top surface (and at most 0.045 m under the top of a separate inner arm); elbow = where the upper-arm line and the forearm line (section centres wrist .. 4 cm under the elbow) meet (midpoint of their closest points) when they make >= 10 deg and meet at 0.38..0.64 of the shoulder -> wrist chord, else at 0.54 of the chord centred in the arm section (solved together, iterated); acromion = top surface 2 cm lateral of the joint

stump.method: no head: the topmost mesh loop is the top of the neck stump; stump.top = bbox centre (x, z) of the vertices in the top 0.02 m, y = the middle of that rim; the column = per 1 cm slice the loops containing the stump axis (the axis follows the narrowest containing loop); stump base = highest slice whose widest containing loop is more than 0.15 m wider than the stump 0.02 m under the top (the shoulder line); Neck = min(stump base, top - 0.09 m), centred in the neck column (the lowest slice at / above it whose innermost containing loop is at most 0.06 m wider than the stump); Head = TECHNICAL joint 0.012 m under the top, centred in the stump (no head geometry)

spine.method: spine joints at 30 / 66 % hip -> neck base (generic heights), x = 0; z at 0.45 of the mid-sagittal depth (|x| < 0.05 m)

symmetry.legs: symmetrised (paired average; one leg length in the pose rig)
symmetry.arms: symmetrised (the two measured sides agree within 0.03 m)

shoulderCutPlanes.method: plane through the cloth-armpit wall point A and the acromion T, containing the front-back axis (zombie/lib/skin.mjs)

labels.method: topology labels on the welded mesh: arm = the arm piece flooded under the cloth armpit + the vertices of the tracked arm loops (sleeve tubes) below the cloth armpit + everything mesh-connected to those below the armpit without passing a vertex of a body (midline-spanning) loop (torn sleeve hems, cuff tatters); leg = the vertices of the leg loops below the crotch

skinning.method: lib/screacher-skin.mjs: regions (arm = topology label below the cloth armpit + outer side of the shoulder cut plane above it; leg = leg-loop label / x sign below the crotch; torso), chain weights with smooth joint blends (zombie/lib/skin.mjs formulas; Neck / Head only inside the stump column, no tilted head boundary), masked Laplacian smoothing on the welded mesh, top 4; small loose components copy the weights of the surface they sit on

mesh.note: the Meshy smart-topology mesh and UVs unchanged (placed: uniform scale + translation); no simplification / re-UV / re-bake; the part-separated shells (clothing, limbs, shoes) keep their own vertices and get position-based weights

clips.method: hand-authored procedural keyframes / gait functions (lib/screacher-clips.mjs) at 30 fps (+ the end time), legs by foot-planting IK (zombie/lib/pose.mjs); not motion capture; the hanging-arm poses are relative to this body's own bind arms

runtime.note: reachM = horizontal root -> right hand tip at the hit frame, actor scale 1 (the hit pose is held over the two 30 fps frames round impactTime); locomotion clips are authored in place for groundSpeed at timeScale 1; Scream returns to the Idle frame-0 pose with the feet planted throughout

attackSolve.method: bisection on the pelvis forward travel of the hit keys (lib/screacher-clips.mjs attackKeys `lunge`) until the CPU-skinned right hand tip is the contract reach from the root in the held hit pose

gait.note: stance travel = groundSpeed x beta x duration (the contract); the pelvis is lowered per variant so the front foot is reached below full leg extension (maxLegReach < 1: no clamped IK, no skating)

deathSolve.method: lib/screacher-clips.mjs solveScreacherDeath (the zombie/lib/clipsolve.mjs coordinate descent + cost, on this body's own supine pose; regions torso incl. the stump, pelvis, arms, legs; NO head term)

floorGuard.method: per frame: Hips raised so the lowest CPU-skinned vertex stays >= 5 mm above the floor (Attack / Hit / Death; not Scream: its feet are planted by IK)

footSkate.method: flat-foot stance frames (Walk: phase 0.15..0.7 x beta, Run: 0.15..0.5 x beta; Idle / Scream: all frames): mean horizontal position of the fixed sole vertex set (bind foot vertices below 3 cm), frame-to-frame speed relative to the treadmill (the stance foot slides back at exactly groundSpeed in place); 0 = no skating; maxSoleTravelM = farthest the planted sole centre ever moves from its first frame

clearance.method: every 2nd frame: CPU-skinned forearm / hand vertices that are uncovered in the bind pose; a ray from the vertex straight away from the posed bone chain the surface wraps (spine chain / nearer leg chain) that hits the posed surface within 0.2 m means the vertex is UNDER that surface: depth = the hit distance. armsVsTorso: forearm / hand vs the torso region above the crotch (clothing shells included); handsVsLegs: hand vs thigh + shin (shorts / trouser legs included). ProbeArmsPressedIn is a synthetic self-check pose (each arm rotated inward about its shoulder until the wrist is over the thigh joint), not a clip

attack.method: CPU skinning of the welded body (top-4 float weights); hand tip = the right-hand-region vertex farthest from the root (feet midpoint, actor origin) horizontally; the hit frame = impactTime with the sampled 30 fps tracks interpolated linearly (slerp) exactly like the runtime; reach = that horizontal distance

motionStretch.method: per triangle: worst edge length ratio posed / bind over every 3rd frame of all seven clips (CPU skinning)

hit.method: torso: 75th pct distance of the torso-region vertices (crotch .. neck base: clothing included) to the Hips-Spine-Chest-Neck chain (capsule Hips -> Neck); limbs: median distance of each limb bone's dominant-weight vertices (middle half of the bone) to its axis, mean of upper + lower and both sides, x1.35 (arm: capsule UpperArm -> Hand) / x1.4 (leg: capsule Thigh -> Foot) like the Strainer / zombie/lib/hit.mjs (unclamped); NO head volume: the stump is not a target

collider.note: contract motor circle radius 0.34 m (ordinary zombie 0.33): the torso / hip / leg core (95th pct horizontal radius 0.226 m; the shoes reach 0.244 m) passes the narrowest walk-through openings (2-cell doors, 1.0 m) with 0.16 m per side; the long hanging arms reach 0.337 m from the axis and may visually brush door jambs (no collision)

contract motor circle radius 0.34 m (ordinary zombie 0.33): the torso / hip / leg core (95th pct horizontal radius 0.226 m; the shoes reach 0.244 m) passes the narrowest walk-through openings (2-cell doors, 1.0 m) with 0.16 m per side; the long hanging arms reach 0.337 m from the axis and may visually brush door jambs (no collision)

torsoCapsule.note: Neck is the base of the stump (the shoulder line): a round-capped capsule Hips -> Neck with the torso radius rises above the top of the stump (capTopIfEndedAtNeck), where a zombie has its head; ending the capsule axis at endYForCapAtStumpTop (= stump top - radius) keeps the cap at the stump top (a runtime choice: stump.top and hitRadii.torso are both in the extras)

notes: torso capsule Hips -> Neck (r torso), limb capsules UpperArm -> Hand (r arm), Thigh -> Foot (r leg); NO head volume (the extras carry no head field): a shot above the shoulders hits nothing
stump.top = the centre of the top of the neck stump in the bind pose (voice / QA anchor, not a target)
all values in model metres at actor root scale 1 (multiply by the runtime scale)

runtime.bones: the same 18 names as the zombie bodies (Root, Hips, Spine, Chest, Neck, Head, L_/R_ UpperArm, Forearm, Hand, Thigh, Shin, Foot)

limitations: Automatic approximate skin weights on a low-poly (16-21 k triangle) source: LBS volume loss at shoulders / elbows / knees in strong poses; no finger bones (the "twitching" and "spread" hands are wrist / forearm motion).
Sleeves, jackets and trouser legs are skinned shells without cloth simulation: where a sleeve hangs against the flank it shears between arm and chest when the arm lifts.
Procedural (not mocap) clips; the knee height is the family proportion (trousers hide the knees of three variants).
Hidden-side geometry and texture of the source are AI-generated (Meshy); the open neck stump shows the generated inside faces.
The long hanging arms swing outside the motor collider (visual brushing of door jambs, no collision change).
Unapproved prototype: appearance, anatomy, deformation, performance and licensing not certified; gameReady false.
rebuild: node --max-old-space-size=3500 tools/asset-pipeline/enemy/build-screacher.mjs [--only <variant>] (needs the private raw masters: SCREACHER_RAW_DIR); QA sheets: node tools/asset-pipeline/enemy/qa/screacher-sheets.mjs
